instructions.name: accept_bid
docs: Seller accepts any open bid on an Open-mode listing, at any time — bids may be above
or below the listing's fair-value snapshot. Auction-mode listings only ever settle
via `settle_auction`, never early.

accounts.name: agent_payout_authority
docs: A bare account reference to `payout_authority(&agent_state)` — see `CreateLaunch`'s
`agent_payout_authority` doc comment for why this indirection exists at all.

instructions.name: cancel_listing
docs: Only a listing with no bids yet can be cancelled — an auction with a bid must run to
expiry (see `settle_auction`).

accounts.name: agent_payout_authority
docs: A bare account reference to `payout_authority(&agent_state)` — see `CreateLaunch`'s
`agent_payout_authority` doc comment for why this indirection exists at all: Anchor's
`associated_token::authority` position only tolerates a bare `<account>.<field>` path
under its separate `idl-build` cfg, not a function call or even a plain ternary (both
compile fine in the real program build, but not there) — routing the computation
through a `constraint = ...` clause instead sidesteps that entirely.

accounts.name: agent_payout_usdc_ata
docs: The agent's earnings destination — its registered `agent_wallet` if set, otherwise
`owner` (see `payout_authority`). Must already exist: the indexer's registrar creates
this ATA once, right after `set_agent_wallet`, the same "system wallet sponsors the
bootstrapping cost" shape the EVM port's gas top-up uses (see agentWalletClaim.ts's
`ensureEvmGasForClaim`) — kept as a plain `mut` rather than `init_if_needed` here
deliberately, since `auto_release_expired` below is permissionless (no Signer to charge
rent to).

accounts.name: agent_payout_authority
docs: A bare account reference to `payout_authority(&agent_state)` — Anchor's `init_if_needed`
associated-token-account codegen needs an actual account it can call `.to_account_info()`
on for the create-ATA CPI, not just a computed `Pubkey` (a plain `mut`-only ATA
constraint, as `ConfirmDelivery`/`AutoReleaseExpired` use, doesn't have this restriction
since it never creates anything — only `init`/`init_if_needed` does). The constraint
below is what actually keeps this trustworthy: the client can pass any account here, but
it must be the agent's real payout authority or the transaction reverts.

accounts.name: creator_token_ata
docs: The creator allocation's destination — the agent's registered wallet if set, otherwise
`creator` itself (== `agent_state.owner`, enforced above) — see `payout_authority`.
`init_if_needed` here doubles as how the agent wallet's own token ATA for this launch's
mint gets created on first use, paid for by `creator` (who's already paying to create
this launch) rather than needing a separate provisioning step.

accounts.name: previous_highest_bid
docs: Present only when this is an Auction listing that already has a highest bid —
that previous-highest bid, refunded here as it's outbid. Omitted by the client for
Open-mode bids or a listing's first Auction bid.

accounts.name: previous_highest_bidder_usdc_ata
docs: Present exactly when `previous_highest_bid` is — the previous bidder's USDC ATA to
refund. Ownership of this account is re-checked in the handler against
`previous_highest_bid.bidder` before any transfer, since the two Optionals can't be
declaratively correlated by Anchor's account-constraint macro.

accounts.name: recipient_authority
docs: A bare account reference to the expected recipient authority — routed through a
`constraint = ...` clause (see `CreateLaunch`'s `agent_payout_authority` doc comment for
why `associated_token::authority` itself can't hold this expression directly).

accounts.name: recipient_usdc_ata
docs: Recipient of the escrow: the agent's payout destination (`payout_authority` — its
registered wallet if set, else `owner`) if releasing to the agent, or the employer's
ATA if refunding. Enforced via `recipient_authority` above rather than trusted from the
caller directly.

instructions.name: set_agent_wallet
docs: One-time-settable: binds `agent_id` to its off-chain-provisioned custodied wallet.
Called by the indexer's registrar signer shortly after the agent registers (see
agentWalletCustody.ts's provisionAgentWallet). Reverts if already set — the wallet is
meant to be a stable, permanent identity for the agent, not reassignable after the fact.

instructions.name: set_registrar
docs: Rotates the authorized registrar signer — e.g. after a key-custody migration.

instructions.name: settle_auction
docs: Permissionless — callable by anyone once the auction's `end_time` has passed, mirroring
`auto_release_expired`'s precedent since no chain can self-execute at a future
timestamp. If the highest bid was withdrawn in the post-end_time race window (see
`withdraw_bid`) or never met the reserve price, the listing simply expires unsold.

accounts.name: highest_bid
docs: Present only if the listing actually received a bid (`highest_bid_id != 0`) — the
winning bid, if the auction is to be settled as a sale.

accounts.name: seller_usdc_ata
docs: Present exactly when `highest_bid` is and its amount met the reserve — the seller's
USDC ATA to pay out. Omitted by the client when settling an unsold/no-bid auction.
Ownership is re-checked in the handler against `listing_state.seller`, same reasoning
as `previous_highest_bidder_usdc_ata` in `PlaceBid`.

instructions.name: withdraw_bid
docs: Always allowed for Open-listing bids and non-highest Auction bids. The
current-highest Auction bid is locked only while the auction is still Active and
before its `end_time` — once that passes, even the highest bidder can reclaim their
funds if nobody has called `settle_auction` yet, so funds can never be stuck behind a
slow keeper (mirrors the EVM exchange's identical withdrawal rule).

types.name: ActiveListingMarker
docs: Tracks whether `agent_id` currently has an active listing, so `create_listing` can
reject a second simultaneous listing for the same agent — a UX/correctness guard, not a
fund-safety one (a stray second listing could never actually settle twice: the second
`accept_bid`/`settle_auction` would fail the `agent_state.owner == listing.seller` check
once the first sale completes). `listing_id == 0` means no active listing.

fields.name: agent_wallet
docs: The agent's own custodied wallet (see packages/custody-core/src/agentWalletCustody.ts),
set once via `set_agent_wallet`. `Pubkey::default()` (all-zero) means "not provisioned
yet" — job payouts and launchpad creator allocations fall back to `owner` until then;
see `payout_authority`.

types.name: BuyerPosition
docs: Tracks how many tokens a wallet has bought from a given launch during the
anti-snipe window. A small standalone PDA per (launch, buyer) so we don't need an
unbounded map inside `LaunchState`.

types.name: ListingState
docs: NFT-style ownership listing for an agent — separate system from `JobState`'s
job-hiring escrow, which this leaves untouched. Unlike the EVM/`ClawdHQAgentExchange`
design, there is no separate "approval" concept here: since the exchange instructions
live in this same program, `create_listing` verifies `agent_state.owner == seller` (and
`accept_bid`/`settle_auction` re-verify it against `listing.seller` before ever writing a
new owner) directly via the same `has_one`/`constraint` pattern `CreateLaunch` already
uses, with no cross-program trust boundary to bridge.

types.name: NameRecord
docs: A marker PDA keyed by `hash(name)` that exists purely to make agent names globally
unique on-chain: `register_agent` uses `init` on this account, which fails if a
record for the same name hash already exists.

fields.name: registrar
docs: The indexer's privileged signer for `set_agent_wallet` — bootstrapped to `authority` as
a placeholder at `initialize()` (the real custody-provisioned wallet doesn't exist yet
at deploy time) and rotated in via `set_registrar` once it does. Mirrors
AgentWalletRegistry.sol's `registrar` on EVM, except Solana has no bytecode-size
pressure forcing it into a separate program — this field lives directly on
`ProtocolState` alongside every other protocol-level authority.

fields.name: exchange_fee_bps
docs: Fee taken from agent-exchange sale proceeds on settlement — independent of
`protocol_fee_bps` (the job-hiring fee), matching the EVM exchange's own separate
`protocolFeeBps` rather than conflating two different fee policies.
